liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Morning Dew** (1 review): Reviewer calls Morning Dew a revelation [10]
- **Big Boss Man** (1 review): Reviewer believes Pigpen played electric piano licks, since no one else plays piano while he plays harp [8]
- **Black Peter** (1 review): Reviewer counts this Black Peter among personal favorites [3]
- **Casey Jones** (1 review): There is a miscommunication among the band at the end of Casey Jones [11]

## The recordings

- **gd1971-06-21.sbd.miller.94356.flac16** (recommended): soundboard; 21 songs; 154 min; rated 4.29/5 by 17 [1]. Said about its sound: Sound is full and rich, with Jerry's subtle playing clear in the mix; The Truckin' intro is cut, and the first few notes of Me And My Uncle are missing [1][10]
- **gd71-06-21.sbd.hanno.4643.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 18 songs; 110 min; rated 3.36/5 by 11 [2]. Said about its sound: Long silences separate most songs on this copy; Sound quality is mediocre; The source has a patch at the beginning, which does not hamper the show [2][3][4][5][8]

## Around the show

- Reviewer saw the show on French television (POP2), which was unheard of back then [4]
- The band played beside a pool ringed with candles at a 450-year-old chateau, around the summer solstice [6]
- Video exists with the Jerry interview, in color for some songs and black and white for others, with French TV commentary [9]
- A free festival was rained out, so the band, staying at a chateau, played behind it for locals [13]
- The chateau is near Auvers, where Van Gogh is buried; the owner was a film composer with a 16-track studio [13]
- Tracks 7-18 are strongly recommended; the earlier tracks are described as optional [8]
- The Charlie Miller transfer is considered better, being a soundboard without patches [9]
- Reviewer ranks it among their all-time great shows [10]
- Reviewer prefers Europe '71 to Europe '72 [11]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1971-06-21.sbd.miller.94356.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Master Reel -> Dat -> CD D [1]. Also: Soundboard from master reel, then unknown step, DAT, then CD; pitch correction applied; discs came from Rob Eaton [1]
- **gd71-06-21.sbd.hanno.4643.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Uli Tuete and Hanno Bunjes; source: Soundboard [2]. Also: Extra tracks before Playin' were filled in using an AM tape, though the patched songs sound weaker [3]
